Triage: lands in apps/console (ApprovalsInboxPage drawer stepper + the RecordDetailView sibling occurrence) — pm:queue, domain:ui, type Bug. Customer-reported on a production 17.1.0 project with live DOM measurements; the reporter has no downstream customization point, so this only gets fixed here. Both occurrences in one card is correct (same component family, same treatment). Dispatch notes for the ui seat: (1) hot-file serial with 5553 (approvals drawer raw-JSON panel) — same ApprovalsInboxPage drawer; answer fold-or-serial explicitly against the five gates before dispatching either (different defect shapes, so serial is the likely answer, but it must be answered, not defaulted); (2) the reporter's explicit ask and their UX read is a vertical stepper — treat that as the recommended route and the layout choice within it (always-vertical vs overflow-triggered) as the dev's implementation judgement; horizontal-with-scroll alone does not meet the requested behaviour. Size/model suggestion: M, opus.

## PM · review of PR #5570 — you measured the vacuity instead of asserting it

Every dev this round was told "the stepper renders" is green against the broken code. You are the only one who **proved** it: a throwaway presence-only probe (`getByLabelText('Approval steps')` plus `getByText` on all six labels) run against the **reverted** component, which **passed 1/1**, then deleted by the same trap and the tree confirmed clean.

That converts my dispatch instruction from an assertion I handed you into a measured fact about this component. It is also the honest way to earn the right to assert the axis/width/scroller contract instead — the naive test isn't rejected on principle, it's rejected on evidence.

### The two occurrences had drifted, which is why one root cause produced two different injuries

I dispatched this as "same component family, same treatment", following triage. You measured that the copies had **already diverged on main**: app-shell carried `overflow-x-auto` + `whitespace-nowrap` + `min-w-4`, console carried none of them. So the same intrinsic-width defect surfaced as *"drags the whole drawer and blanks the panel"* in one host and *"scrolls itself, tail steps behind an unmarked gesture"* in the other. Neither the card nor my dispatch had that; it is the reason the fix had to be written twice rather than once. **#5569** filed for the duplication, correctly cross-linking #2763 as the larger thing that would subsume it.

### The layout ruling, and why "no threshold" is the stronger claim

Always-vertical with no breakpoint, no `ResizeObserver`, no count branch — so the layout is viewport-invariant and flow-length-invariant **by construction rather than by sampling**. The suites pin that directly: no breakpoint-prefixed axis / overflow / width-pinning class anywhere in the subtree, and layout classes byte-identical across a 2/5/6/12 sweep. Sampling two viewports could never prove the absence of a bad breakpoint; this does.

Using the reporter's own CJK labels verbatim is load-bearing and you said why: 8–16 CJK characters is roughly double the rendered width of the same count in English, so English fixtures would have quietly moved the fixture out of the failing regime.

### The limitation you declared, accepted as declared

**Viewports were not sampled** — chromium is absent from the container (`Executable doesn't exist at /opt/pw-browsers/…`), and you claim no real-layout measurement. I had independently flagged exactly this gap before your report arrived: the assertions are Tailwind class-contract proxies, and the original defect was measured in a real browser (1070px inside 527px). Stating it as a limitation rather than dressing it as coverage is the right call, and the class tokens are each named for the CSS property that caused the overflow, so the proxy is tight. `Live E2E` runs in CI regardless. Not a blocker — recorded so the residual is visible rather than implied.

`check:doc-snippets` first exiting 1 on an unbuilt `@object-ui/cli` was correctly diagnosed as a broken-gauge precondition rather than a finding, fixed by building and re-running, and **recorded so the first red is not misread later**. Same discipline as round 1's `check:eager-closure` incident.

### Sanitizer: the characterization just got sharper, and it changes the fix

Three measured instances now, and yours refines it. The literal-text marker **survived** — so the workaround holds. But the sanitizer still ate two **angle-bracket placeholders** (`<both components>`, `<both>`) inside your report body.

So the defect is not "HTML comments are stripped". It is **angle-bracket-delimited content is stripped**, which is why `<!-- os-dev-report -->` dies *and* why JSX tags vanish from issue code blocks — you correctly identified that same behaviour in #5554's own body and distinguished it from truncation when checking completeness, which is exactly the trap that discipline exists to catch.

That materially changes the skills-lane item: the remedy is not merely "pick a different marker", it is that **any report carrying JSX, generics, or angle-bracket placeholders loses content silently**. I am carrying that up with all three instances.

### Status

Path surface verified via `get_files`: 5 files, `apps/console/**` + `packages/app-shell/**` + the changeset — exactly the **amended** fence, no breach, no governed surface. CI on #5570 has not converged; no verdict and no enqueue until the gate jobs read `completed: success` by name.
